text:
Nearly 300 games into his Islanders career, Simon Holmstrom is finally getting a feature role. He is playing 18:24 a night (16:44 last season), is on the ice for 48% of the Islanders' power-play chances (19% last season), and has 12 points in 18 games. Over his last ten he is averaging nearly 20 minutes.

The breakout looks mostly earned. His own chances are up to 0.92 expected goals per 60 from 0.66, the Islanders win the chance battle at five on five with him on (53% of expected goals, 4 points better than without him), and the luck around him is close to neutral. The one stretch is his shooting: 18.2%, a touch above the top of our range, so a cooler month would not mean the role has gone.

His turnaround snipe 39 seconds into the third period in Los Angeles on Thursday showed the finishing touch. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries last season; watch whether that keeps him on the top unit.
